cards.text: Jesus crosses back over the sea by boat, and a large crowd gathers around Him right there on the shore. Then a synagogue leader named Jairus arrives. He sees Jesus and falls at His feet.

cards.question: Jairus falls at Jesus' feet and pleads with Him urgently. What's going on back at his house?

answers.text: His little daughter is near death
His young son is sick with fever
His servant is paralyzed in bed

cards.question: Jairus begs Jesus, “Please come and place Your ___ on her, so that she will be healed and live.”

cards.text: So Jesus goes with him, and a large crowd follows, pressing in around Him. Friend, I spent YEARS squeezed between takeout menus in a junk drawer, and even I'd call that tight.
Somewhere in that crowd is a woman who has suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She's been through much agony under many physicians, and she's spent all she had.

cards.question: After all those physicians and all that money, the woman's condition got better.

cards.text: Then she hears about Jesus. No big entrance. She just works her way through the crowd and comes up behind Him.

cards.question: The woman has made it through the crowd and is right behind Jesus. What does she do?

answers.text: She takes hold of His hand

cards.question: Why the cloak? The woman kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be ___.”
The woman touches Jesus' cloak. What happens to her bleeding?

answers.text: It slows over a few days
It stops once she gets home

cards.text: Twelve years, and she can feel it in her body. She's HEALED! And at once, Jesus is aware that power has gone out from Him.

cards.question: Jesus knows power has gone out from Him, and He turns to the crowd. What does He ask?

answers.text: Who is in need of healing

cards.question: When Jesus asks who touched His garments, His disciples point right to the woman.

cards.text: Instead they point at the crowd pressing in on Him and ask how He can say, ‘Who touched Me?’ Fair point, guys, that's like asking who bumped you in a packed elevator at rush hour.

cards.question: After the disciples answer, Jesus lets the question drop and moves on.

cards.text: Knowing what happened to her, the woman comes and falls down before Him, trembling in fear. I shook like that every single time somebody opened the junk drawer.

cards.question: Trembling, the woman falls down before Jesus. What does she tell Him?
Jesus scolds the woman for touching His cloak.
Jesus tells her: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your ___ has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.”

cards.text: Jesus is still speaking to the woman when messengers arrive from the house of Jairus, the synagogue leader. Remember, back home his little daughter was near death.

cards.question: Messengers from Jairus's house reach him in the crowd. What news do they bring?

answers.text: His daughter is asking for him

cards.text: And they add, “why bother the Teacher anymore?” Friend, I bet Jairus felt the floor drop right out from under him.

cards.question: Jesus overhears what the messengers told Jairus. What does Jesus tell him?

answers.text: Not to be afraid but just believe
To go home and wait for Him
To call his family together to pray

cards.question: Jesus lets the whole crowd come with Him to Jairus's house.

cards.text: Only Peter, James, and John the brother of James go with Him, three of His disciples. After that crowd, three people must feel like a whole empty bakery.
They reach the synagogue leader's house, and it's a commotion. People are weeping and wailing loudly.

cards.question: Jesus walks into all that weeping and wailing. What does He say about the girl?

answers.text: She is not dead but asleep
She is gone beyond all help
She will be healed by morning

cards.question: When Jesus says the child is not dead but asleep, the people there ___ at Him.
Jesus lets everyone in the house stay and watch while He goes in to see the girl.

cards.text: Jesus puts them all outside. Laugh at Jesus, and you're watching from outside.
He takes the child's father and mother and His three companions in to see her. Then He takes her by the hand and says, “Talitha koum!”

cards.question: Holding the girl's hand, Jesus says “Talitha koum!” What does it mean?

answers.text: Little girl I say to you get up
Little girl rest now in peace
Little girl your father is here

cards.question: When Jesus tells her to get up, the girl immediately gets up and begins to walk around.

cards.text: And at once, they are utterly astounded. Friend, I've read this a hundred times and I'm STILL astounded.

cards.question: Mark tucks in the girl's age, and it's a number that already came up earlier in this passage. She was ___ years old.

cards.text: Then Jesus gives strict orders that no one should know about this.

cards.question: Jesus gives one more instruction about the girl. What is it?

cards.text: She was dead, now she's walking around, and Jesus' next instruction is basically: get this girl something to eat. That's the most Papa move I have EVER seen.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "Please come and place Your ___ on her, so that she will be healed and live.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "If only I touch His garments, I will be ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 19 quotes "your ___ has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question names the speaker twice: "Jesus tells her: “Daughter,” said Jesus, ...". The setup and the quote say the same thing, so the question reads awkwardly.

The card calls Peter, James and John "three of His disciples." That fact comes from outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Mark 5:37, which doesn't call them disciples.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke "three people must feel like a whole empty bakery" doesn't click. It isn't clear how three people could feel like an empty bakery, so a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "Laugh at Jesus, and you're watching from outside" makes their laughing the reason Jesus puts them outside. Mark 5:40 doesn't say why He put them out.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "I've read this a hundred times and I'm STILL astounded" is a pleasant reaction, not a real laugh, at one of the biggest moments in the passage.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says the girl's age is "a number that already came up earlier in this passage." The wrong answer "three" also came up earlier: cards 6 and 12 of this stop both say "three" for Peter, James and John. A baker could argue "three" fits the hint.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The last card retells what card 18 already covered: she gets up, she walks around, give her something to eat. It adds a joke but doesn't move the passage forward, so it's a recap card.
The card tells Mark 5:42 ("now she's walking around") as well as 5:43, but it cites only Mark 5:43.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says "She was dead" as a fact. In Mark's text, only the messengers say she is dead (5:35), and Jesus says "The child is not dead, but asleep" (5:39). Mark never states it in his own voice.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin state that Jairus's daughter was dead, or should he keep to what the people in the passage said, like "They said she was dead"?
